articleTitle: Design and test of VSC assisted resonant current (VARC) DC circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper presents the VSC assisted resonant current (VARC) direct current circuit-breaker concept, which comprises a vacuum interrupter, operated by an ultra-fast actuator, together with a power electronic converter that creates a zero-crossing in the arc current. A few main circuit topologies are shown and discussed and a dynamic model of the DC link voltage in the VSC is presented. A module rated for 10 kA against 40 kV transient interruption voltage has been built and tested at an independent test laboratory, and some test results are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of harmonic transfer through an MVDC link
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The impact of harmonics and resonances on the medium voltage direct current (MVDC) link embedded in the Anglesey 33 kV distribution networks is evaluated in this paper. The background harmonics at either end of the MVDC link is analysed to identify dominant harmonic components. The ac to dc conversion is evaluated with focus on the dc link topology and its harmonic behaviour. This is followed with a detailed power electronic converter switching model implementation for harmonic transfer studies. The modelling aspects resemble the proposed Angle DC converters as close as reasonably practicable. To align with this objective cascaded three level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC)-based MVDC link has been implemented in the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform. The MVDC link is in symmetrical monopole configuration capable of operating at bipolar voltages, resembling the Angle DC link operation. Furthermore, the analysis focused on the different dc link configuration and their behaviour to ac system background harmonics. The results show potential harmonic transfer through the MVDC link.

articleTitle: AC fault dynamic studies of islanded grid including HVDC links operating in VF-control
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: VSC-HVDC link can operate in VF-control (or grid-forming mode) when connected to a weak or islanded network to overcome the PQ-control (or grid-feeding) limitation. Up to now, the VF-control represents a challenge due to static and dynamic limits. This paper provides a dynamic performance, during AC faults, of HVDC link in VF-control connected to an islanded grid. The islanded grid is based on the Northern France network and includes synchronous generator and wind farm. The EMT-type simulations provides an insight on dynamic network behavior when HVDC is operating in VF-control.

articleTitle: The series bridge converter: A compact and economic VSC-HVDC converter
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Recent experience has revealed that Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology is the preferred solution for offshore HVDC power transmission due to its inherent advantages. The drive to reduce overall cost and size of the offshore HVDC platform has challenged this segment of the industry to explore different VSC topologies. This paper presents the benefits of the Series Bridge Converter (SBC), with key focus on power losses, cost, weight, footprint, and volume. Its performance in these areas is compared to that of the Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC).

articleTitle: Parallel operation of HVDC DRU and VSC converters for offshore wind farm connection: Technical and economic feasibility
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In the current research, innovative connection concepts using different HVDC converter technologies that can offer cost reduction potential were developed and the technical and economic feasibility of a selected topology was investigated. A parallel operation of DRU and VSC topology was modelled in PSCAD/EMTDC in order to assess its behavior in normal as well as transient operation modes. Two active power flow control schemes were developed to control the active power sharing between the DRU and VSC converters. The results show that the VSC provides ancillary services and supports the DRU which makes this concept technically feasible. Moreover, the cost analysis showed a cost reduction potential for this hybrid topology of 8–20 % depending on the scenario over a lifetime of 30 years.

articleTitle: Study of the impact of DC-DC converters on the protection strategy of HVDC grids
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: HVDC grids are expected to be a solution to upgrade the existing AC system. However, their development presents several technical challenges like power flow control, grid protection and interconnection of grids with different technology or voltage levels. One required technology for the development of such grids is the DC-DC converter capable of operating at hundreds of kilovolts and hundreds of megawatts. While different DC-DC converter topologies have been proposed in literature, most studies focus on the topology itself and there is a lack of studies that deal with their grid integration. This paper studies the role of DC-DC converters in the protection of HVDC grids acting as firewalls to stop the propagation of faults. The effects of blocking the converter or actively controlling its operation during faults are presented. The results demonstrate the capabilities of DC-DC converters beyond DC voltage transformation.

articleTitle: Impact of synchronous machine dynamics on the stability of a power grid with high penetration of variable renewable energies
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to investigate interactions between a Current Control mode Inverter (CCI) and an Equivalent Synchronous Machine (ESM) representing the frequency and voltage dynamics of the power grid. The stability limit of the system as a function of the Power Ratio (PR) between the CCI and ESM and the electrical distance between both was identified using a method proposed in this paper. Furthermore, the impact of the operating point of the CCI on the stability limits of the system was also investigated.

articleTitle: Cost analysis and comparison between modular multilevel converter (MMC) and modular multilevel matrix converter (M3C) for offshore wind power transmission
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper focuses on the cost analysis of offshore wind power system using Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) based HVDC or Modular Multilevel Matrix Converter (M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>C) based fractional frequency transmission (FFT). Capital investment and long-term costs due to unavailability, Operation & Maintenance and power loss are analysed. The total cost is broken down into elements and those have larger impact on the overall cost are highlighted. Cost comparison between the two technologies is presented. Economical breakeven distance is analysed for schemes with different power ratings. In addition, sensitivity analysis is conducted considering discount rate, energy price, capacity factor, wind farm life time and wind turbine type to gain insight into the overall cost.

articleTitle: DC-DC transformer for interconnecting HVDC grids of different technologies and grounding schemes into an HVDC multi-terminal grid
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In this paper, a new DC-DC transformer topology is described and analyzed. The Modular Multilevel DC Transformer (MMDCT) is studied for interconnecting high-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems with different grounding schemes and converter technologies. Its operating principle is explained and demonstrated using time-domain simulations, where the MMDCT is connected to a hybrid HVDC system with a Line Commutated Converter (LCC) based system on one side and to a Voltage Source Converter (VSC) based system, specifically a Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) to the other.

articleTitle: On control and balancing of MMC-HVdc links in rigid bipolar configuration
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: For bulk power transmission high voltage direct current schemes based on modular multilevel converter technology offer a high flexibility and reliability. This is especially valid, if bipolar schemes with dedicated metallic return or rigid bipolar configurations are utilized. In case of the latter configuration a floating neutral bus between positive and negative converter exists at one terminal. Therefore, new challenges in control and system design arise. While bipolar configurations with dedicated metallic return are well studied, investigations on the rigid bipolar configuration have been rarely addressed in literature. This paper presents the main differences as well as characteristic control and balancing aspects of the rigid bipolar configuration.

articleTitle: FMEA of a non-selective fault-clearing strategy for HVDC grids
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The Failure Mode Effect Analysis (FMEA) is a technique used to investigate failures in a process or component and to identify the resultant effects of these failures on system operations. In this paper it is explained how the FMEA can be used to define and assess the impact of the failure modes (FM) of a protection strategy for High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) grids. The risk assessment of HVDC protection strategies is important because, despite of being very unlikely, the occurrence of failures during the fault clearing can cause impacts of great severity to the system. Equations for the likelihood and methods to measure the severity of FMs are discussed in the paper. A non-selective protection strategy is used to illustrate the method and the meaning of the risks assessed are discussed.

articleTitle: Preventive coordination of active power set-points and DC voltage control for enhanced N-1 security in mixed AC-HVDC-systems
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: At present, N-1 security of AC-HVDC-systems is evaluated separately for both the AC and HVDC system. The application of Voltage Source Converters (VSCs) ensures a controlled power exchange between both systems. This enables a combined system operation and therefore a combined security assessment of both systems. This work proposes a Preventive Security Constrained Optimal Power Flow (PSCOPF), which adapts VSC set-points (pVSC and uDC) and their droop gain of the DC voltage control in order to increase the overall system security by minimizing the number of critical contingencies. Thereby, all possible equipment outages are considered in the N-1 analysis. The PSCOPF method is based on a Differential Evolution algorithm. Furthermore, it is investigated if VSC set-points and droop gains can be optimised simultaneously or in a staggered approach.

articleTitle: Small signal state space model of the frequency-dependent DC cable based on direct vector fitting
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper proposes a new method to represent transmission lines and cables in state space. The method accounts for the frequency dependency of line parameters and essentially translates the state of the art time-domain universal line model into state space. The proposed model is compared against the latest state space model for single DC cable and a bipolar DC cable and it shows certain advantages. DC cables are represented without applying Kron reduction which means that a higher accuracy can be achieved. Single DC cable is represented with a lower model order and higher accuracy for a wide spectre of upper frequency limits and cable lengths. The longer the cable and the higher the upper frequency limit, the more pronounced is the model order reduction. The two state space models are also compared for a 70km bipolar DC cable in the frequency range up to 1 kHz and the proposed model achieves higher accuracy with a slightly lower model order. More importantly, the proposed model succeeds at representing the effect of mutual coupling within the desired accuracy criteria. Furthermore, based on the analysis of the two-conductor DC cable (bipolar cable), it is shown that the proposed method overcomes the issue to represent unbalanced multi-conductor lines and cables in state space. The reason is that it avoids modal transformation. Moreover, in case of multi-conductor lines and cables, it is expected that the proposed method is beneficial for longer systems, higher upper frequency limits and for more mutually coupled conductors.

articleTitle: Mathematical harmonic model of VSC HVDC for offshore applications
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: HVDC transmission with Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) technology is frequently used for connection to weak offshore grids. In such systems, adverse harmonic resonances and instabilities can occur due to the interaction between the different power electronic converters and the grid. Models of the HVDC converters describing their harmonic behaviour are needed by HVDC manufacturers at design stage and they are required by Transmission System Operators to allow prediction of such interactions and their impact on the grid. This paper describes one such model. It aims to be a comprehensive tool to analyse and predict harmonic interactions combining the control system, normally represented in dq frame, and the power system, normally analysed in the positive-negative sequence frame. This methodology can be applied to any device connected to the power system to capture key aspects of harmonic interaction including cross-coupling between harmonic frequencies. Moreover, such a tool will enable design of robust control systems. The process described in this paper is applied to a typical MMC-HVDC converter connected to an offshore grid. The mathematical model is validated through PSCAD simulation, and a practical case study is shown.

articleTitle: Internal model design for power electronic controllers
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Designing controllers for power electronic applications to meet high performance standards can be challenging as there can be many internal and external conditions that are not well accounted for. Factors such as system parameter changes, system operating condition changes, filtering, and delays in the measurements, may adversely affect the performance of a circuit in which the controller design is not immune to such disturbances. In this paper, the internal model design concept is explored as a viable approach for designing controllers with improved performance despite system variations. A new control strategy that improves the stability of a voltage source converter (VSC) using the internal model design concept is discussed. Conclusions show that the proposed control system can positively influence the overall dynamic response and offers better controllability despite unexpected system variations, compared to a classical decoupled control system.

articleTitle: Coupling of HV distributions systems through multiple point-to-point-DC-connections
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In more and more countries conventional power plants based on fossil fuels are being substituted gradually by renewable energy sources (RES) like wind turbines, photovoltaics, biogas power plants etc., which affects the other both sectors. Because of varying weather conditions, the feed-in of RES shifts temporally as well as geographically and makes a secure system operation more difficult. A second important aspect is that a significant number of those RES are predominantly connected to the distribution grid levels. The ratio of feed-in to load is very different in distribution systems so that the balancing usually takes place via the transmission grid. However, the increase in bottlenecks in the transmission grids is hindering the balancing. Frequent shutdowns of RES units are the result. This contribution represents a new approach to power balancing at the same voltage level. The objective is to integrate several point-to-point direct current (DC) couplings into the distribution system operation so that additional power transits between high-feed and high-load network groups are possible. The concept is shown in Figure 1. The DC links can be executed as DC-lines or as Back-2-Back converters, which is not further distinguished in this contribution.

articleTitle: Development of HVDC offshore grids in the European system: Long-term transmission expansion analyses
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper provides an assessment to optimise the development of HVDC offshore grids in the North Seas in a 2050 time horizon. This is carried out by the application of a specific approach to find the global optimum between the development of offshore and onshore corridors in the North Seas region at 2050.

articleTitle: Extracting artificial inertia from a HVDC transmission scheme
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper discusses the energy stored in a HVDC cable and the extraction of this energy using MMC based on either fullbridge or half-bridge converters. By using the reactive power absorption capability of a half-bridge converter, a method of increasing the, otherwise, limited depth of the DC voltage reduction achievable is discussed.

articleTitle: Development of a small-signal assessment tool for multi-terminal LCC schemes
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: A linearized model of a three-terminal HVDC system based on Manitoba Hydro BPII HVDC line parameters is developed, which includes three LCC converter models, one three-terminal HVDC line model, three phase locked loop (PLL) models and three HVDC controller models (one voltage controller and two current controllers). It was benchmarked with the Electromagnetic Transient Simulation program PSCAD/EMTDC. The results demonstrate that the developed small-signal model can be used to analyse MTHVDC interactions. The paper recommends that a small­signal interaction study should be performed to identify any interactions between the controllers of MTHVDC systems.

articleTitle: Vector fitting-based reduced order modelling method for power cables
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: To study the frequency and damping characteristics of power cable, high-order RLC circuit models are commonly required, which involves high computational burdens for modelling and analysis. In this paper, a reduced-order modelling method for power cable is proposed on the basis of Prony analysis (PA), vector fitting (VF) algorithm and balanced truncation (BT) algorithm. The state space model of power cable is first obtained by fitting terminal frequency responses using PA and VF instead of directly building mathematical model; Then the low-frequency characteristics is maintained using BT algorithm. The fitting accuracy can be improved by increasing the order. The proposed method is able to reduce computational burdens for power cable modelling, which thus improves modelling and analysis efficiency. Simulation results are given to validate the effectiveness of the proposed modelling method.

articleTitle: Controlling a 33 kV flexible power link in GB's distribution network
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In Great Britain, Western Power Distribution is trialling an AC-DC-AC power electronics-based "Flexible Power Link" to interconnect two areas of 33 kV distribution network, balancing real power flows and providing voltage support. This paper describes the control module that is used to dispatch setpoints to the Flexible Power Link to alleviate network violations, based on visibility of conditions within the wider distribution network.

articleTitle: A novel control strategy for frequency and voltage support from off-shore wind farm through HVDC links
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In this paper, a new control strategy — Frequency-based Synchronization Control (FSC) is applied to a Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) HVDC system which is used to integrate off-shore wind farms to an on-shore ac system. A detailed electromagnetic model is set up to evaluate the HVDC dynamic performance under the new control strategy in different contingencies. The results show a converter with FSC control can provide better inertial and voltage support to ac system.

articleTitle: Lifetime estimation and performance evaluation for offshore wind farms transmission cables
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: A novel methodology for life estimation and performance evaluation of offshore wind farms high voltage AC export cables is presented. The method applies Dynamic Temperature Prediction (DTP) analysis using a Thermo-Electrical Equivalent model (TEE). Furthermore, it is suggested how the cable lifetime might be inferred based on the accumulated ageing effects. Afterwards, a sensitivity analysis of the seabed temperature variations is performed. Finally, a holistic procedure for calculating more accurately the electrical power losses of the cable is presented. Results show that an important increase of the total installed power, or cross-section reduction, can be achieved compared to traditional sizing methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of maximum power transfer capability of a hybrid modular multilevel converter
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper presents a study on evaluating the power transfer capability of a novel hybrid cascaded modular multilevel voltage source converter topology. The configuration utilizes third harmonic injection to enable reactive power compensation by varying the ac side converter voltage in the presence of constant dc side voltage. The maximum converter voltage is determined by the number and rating of submodules and triplen harmonic compensation whereas the maximum allowable steady current through the converter determines its MVA rating. These constraints must be considered in determining the maximum power transfer capability of this converter configuration, connected to strong and weak ac buses. Further the reactive power required to be supplied by the converter under this condition is evaluated for these different system strengths. Results obtained from a developed Electro-Magnetic Transient (EMT) simulation model are presented in this paper, for validation of the theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: Bipolar fault performance analysis and protection solutions in VSC-MTDC system
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The increasing deployment of decentralized renewable energy sources, and the long transmission distances between the generation sources and the load centres bring new challenges to the conventional AC grids, the VSC-HVDC grid is considered to be a better alternative. In order to increase the reliability of VSC-MTDC system, this work is to investigate a fast fault locating algorithm considering utilization of the rate of rise of current (di/dt) and the rate of decline of voltage (dv/dt) and high DC fault current breaking capability of DC circuit breaker to isolate and clear the fault rapidly. A five-terminal radial VSC HVDC network model is established using PSCAD Platform to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Fault behaviour of bipolar overhead line based HVDC grids
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper provides a fault analysis of bipolar overhead line based HVDC grids using HB-MMC converters. The impacts of fault type and fault resistance are shown and the physical behaviour of the transient fault return current is explained. A transformation in modal quantities enables a decoupling of the measured phase currents and voltages. The results are presented in a Point-to-Point HVDC grid for both phase and modal quantities. It is shown that fault analysis in the modal domain is an auspicious method for fault detection and faulty line discrimination.

articleTitle: A priori error estimation of the structure-preserving modal model reduction by state residualization of a grid forming converter for use in 100% power electronics transmission systems
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This article deals with the model order reduction by state residualization of power electronic converters. It presents a method to a priori estimate the error induced by this reduction. This method helps choosing the most suitable reduced model, the one that minimizes the error, depending on the simulated events. When applied to a system with several converters, it helps choosing which converter to reduce and how much, in order to simplify the models while keeping a sufficient accuracy.

articleTitle: Tank test circuit for fast DC circuit-breakers
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Several concepts have been proposed for fast-acting DC circuit-breakers (DC CB) based on mechanical current-interrupters assisted by power electronic auxiliary circuitry, which creates a zero-crossing in the current through the interrupter. Most often a vacuum interrupter (VI) is used. Desired operation time is maximum a few milliseconds. In this paper we will discuss possible arrangements to perform preliminary relevant testing of the current breaking and the voltage withstand capability in a development laboratory environment.

articleTitle: Impact of MTDC grid reconfiguration and control on the dynamics of the GB system
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids are becoming increasingly popular for interconnecting non-synchronous generating resources such as offshore wind power plants (WPPs). The benefit of MTDC systems is that they can be reconfigured during contingencies to maintain the supply of power to the host AC systems. DC grid reconfiguration in MTDC systems will inevitably change the power injections to the host AC system, and will thus affect the dynamic behaviour of the AC system. This paper investigates the dynamic behaviour of the representative Great British (GB) transmission system (i.e. a reduced order dynamic model) for a series of reconfigurations in a meshed MTDC grid connecting offshore WPPs to the system. Hierarchical control strategies for the MTDC system including a DC power flow solver (PFS) and pilot voltage droop (PVD) are compared. From the analysis, it is observed that the reconfiguration of MTDC grid has a notable impact on large-disturbance dynamics of the GB transmission system.

articleTitle: Methodology for state-space modelling of power electronic elements in modern electrical energy systems
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper introduces a methodology to analytically obtain a small-signal model of power systems including power electronic devices. By using the Component Connection Method, the overall system can be partitioned into individual subsystems that are modelled separately in state-space, simplifying the ana­lytical description and featuring modular modelling advantages. The system components are coupled by means of sparse linking matrices to an overall closed-loop system used for modal-based linear analysis. This methodology is applied to obtain a small­signal model of a VSC-HVDC system. Using eigenvalue and eigenvector analysis, the dynamics of the VSC-HVDC link can be examined in detail. Weak grid interconnection is addressed by means of a sensitivity analysis, The generic linearized model is then benchmarked with a time domain large-signal reference model of the VSC-HVDC.

articleTitle: Novel partial power flow solver for multi — terminal HVDC control
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Accurate control of the power flowing through multi-terminal HVDC networks is necessary to ensure that maximum power is being absorbed from the offshore windfarms. The current literature implements a Power Flow Solver to achieve this control. However, it requires knowledge of the entire network and measurements from each converter. In this paper, a novel power flow solver is presented which only requires measurements from the converters directly connected to the converter of interest. This partial Power Flow Solver (partial PFS) proves to be robust, having lower measurement requirements and consistently achieves tracking within 10% of the power setpoint for the cases considered. The partial PFS was employed on a 5-Terminal simplified state-space VSC-HVDC network model that integrates windfarm generation, an offshore passive load, and onshore grid connected Converters. Both fibre-optic and satellite communication ware considered for the control of the PFS. Preliminary tests of the partial PFS under severe system operation showed that it had an acceptable response for both communication options. An upgraded partial PFS was also presented which increases the controller's accuracy.

articleTitle: An initiative for modelling DC grids for large scale transient stability studies
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: As an initiative for the DC grids, this paper presents a multi-terminal HVDC model in which the DC terminals can be connected using radial or meshed connections. The model has been developed for Manitoba Hydro in order to assess the large scale transient stability related issues of the future plan of having multiple HVDC taps on its HVDC Bipole III. A two-time step modelling approach, which allows the DC portion of the stability model to be run at a smaller time step has been used and therefore the control details and DC network dynamics have been represented accurately. The validation results against an EMT model and the model performance in a very large power system model are also presented.

articleTitle: Improved droop control with DC grid resonance damping capability
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The concept of the so-called droop control has been widely discussed in the literature as the preferred controller for Voltage Source Converter for High Voltage Direct Current (VSC-HVDC) multiterminal and DC grid schemes. Droop control provides fast dynamic response and power-sharing between converter stations among other advantages but, as the controller is usually implemented as a merely proportional gain, the DC grid resonances damping is often very poor. This is because although the grids under study are DC, a broad range of high-frequency components and transient dynamics are inevitable in DC grids caused by long cables and switching to name a few. Conventional droops based on proportional gain are not able to handle such frequency-dependant issues of the DC grids. To improve the DC dynamic response, this paper presents a new droop controller where a DC resonance mitigation compensator is augmented to the conventional droop control that will result in an improved droop compensation by guaranteeing that power-sharing task will satisfactorily meet the desired damping requirements.

articleTitle: A comparative study of master-slave control and virtual synchronous machine control for parallel VSC-HVDC links feeding passive loads on offshore platforms
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The paper investigates the supply of power to an offshore oil/gas platform from two separate VSC links of different ratings. Two different types of VSC control strategies were considered — a Master-Slave (M/S) control strategy where the master converter controls the ac voltage and frequency, and the slave its own power output; and a Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM) control strategy, where both converters emulate synchronous machines. Load balancing, start-up of offshore induction motors, transfer and tripping of loads in case of failure of one of the links, and fault recovery and ride-through are discussed. It is seen that the VSM control can be implemented without any communication between the links. On the other hand, the M/S control requires communication and an additional Power Management Allocator (PMA) but is inherently better at current limiting.

articleTitle: A new islanding detection method for grid-connected photovoltaic system based on harmonic impedance sequence component
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of the existing islanding detection methods, the relationship between the structural features and fault characteristics of photovoltaic power generation system, and the difference between normal grid-connected operation and islanding operation are studied in this paper. According to the difference, a new principle about the anti-islanding protection is proposed, which is implemented by using impedance characteristic frequency sequence components and has no detecting blind area. The principle can quickly identify islanding state by detecting impedance component at the PCC point even in the case of single-phase and two-phase disconnection, and it can not affect the quality of power system. The simulation results show that this method can effectively detect the island and has no detection zones. And it's response is fast and has no impact on the power quality.

articleTitle: Adaptive energy filters smoothing renewable power fluctuations at different power levels
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Renewable energy is playing an increasingly important role in modern and future power system. However, most of renewables (wind, solar and wave) have huge power fluctuations, which cause frequency variations, voltage flickers, forced oscillations, thermal excursions and wasted capacities of equipments and generally undermine the system stability. In previous works, energy filters are proposed to smooth renewable power fluctuations without input power measurements. However, conventional controls of energy filters require good estimations of average input power levels to manage energy storage systems. In this paper, a new control method is proposed to make energy filters adaptive to the change of input power levels, which is no longer estimated as a constant but is given by an adaptation law in real time. Proposed control laws are comparatively studied with conventional energy filter controls in terms of their filter responses, ESS responses and parameters selection. The proposed adaptive energy filters are demonstrated based on RTDS simulations. Results show that adaptive energy filters are able to smooth renewable power fluctuations and meanwhile regulate its energy storage level when the input power level changes.

articleTitle: Small-signal dynamics of MMC based DC-grid system
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of MMC based DC-grid system dynamics using small-signal analysis techniques. A dynamic-phasor based linearized DC-grid model is developed considering the internal harmonics of MMC, and the model-verification is conducted by electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC. Based on eigenvalue analysis, the poorly-damped oscillatory modes, which has higher possibility to induce system instability, are identified and categorized into four types, i.e., 1) DC network interaction mode, 2) MMC internal harmonic mode, 3) converter and AC-system interaction mode and 4) AC-system and controller interaction mode. The obtained results reveal various interaction phenomena among the AC-systems, MMCs, DC network and the controllers of DC-grid system, which could provide useful guidance for system-design and parameter-selection in MMC based DC-grid field.

articleTitle: Analysis of the variables influencing inter-area oscillations in the future Great Britain power system
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The integration of power electronics (PE) interfaced resources in electrical power systems has been growing continuously. In future power systems, PE-interfaced devices, including renewable energy resources (RES) and High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) technologies, are going to play a significant role in providing electrical energy. Therefore, the study of power system stability in mixed AC/DC networks is of critical importance. A significant number of wind and HVDC technologies will be connected to the Great Britain (GB) network by 2030, which makes the network an interesting study into the stability of mixed AC/DC networks with high numbers of PE-interfaced sources. In this paper, a reduced-order model of the future GB network is developed and used as a study case to explore the factors influencing the damping of an inter-area oscillation. The system variables are measured and a new measure, the centre of inertia (COI) electrical distance, is developed based on graph theory concepts to quantify changes in network topology. Then, correlation analysis is performed between these indices and the damping ratios of an inter-area oscillation. The results show that the new index, COI electrical distance, has a strong correlation with the damping of inter-area oscillation under changes in the network topology, which can be used for quick identification of potentially problematic operational scenarios.

articleTitle: Interoperability of different voltage source converter topologies in HVDC grids
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed study of DC grid operation using a range of user-defined offline and real-time HVDC converter models which were rigorously validated against offline and real-time benchmarks. Provided that these models are destined for use in real-time hardware in the loop simulation and a wide range of offline system studies, this paper assesses their suitability for studying complex DC grids that consist of multiple voltage source converters which differ in their control range and fault ride-through capabilities. Detailed quantitative studies show that the offline and real-time DC grid models produce well matched results and provide efficient approaches to investigate DC grid operation during normal condition and AC and DC faults.

articleTitle: DC grid demonstration to verify the control flexibility of the grid connected with renewable power generation and energy storage
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper presents a four terminal bipolar DC grid demonstrator, composed of two VSCs and two DC/DC converters in a loop topological structure. The wind and photovoltaic power generations together with battery energy storage are connected with the DC grid through three converters respectively, in order to demonstrate the control flexibility of the grid-connected fluctuated renewables and its shaving using energy storage. The DC grid demonstration system is built in the laboratory environment with homothetic design in terms of the actual HVDC project data, and the corresponding coordinated control strategies on system voltage and power are studied. A SCADA system to monitor and control the DC grid is designed and developed. A series of operational and control scenarios of the DC grid are studied and verified, such as the start-up and shutdown of the DC grid, multi-sources hybridoperation, shaving power fluctuations, wind generation shutdown and single-polar failure, etc. Those scenarios are also compared with the results obtained from the MATLAB/Simulink software simulations.

articleTitle: An analysis of the impact of an advanced aero-hydro-servo-elastic model of dynamics on the generator-converter dynamics, for an offshore fixed 5MW PMSG wind turbine
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper gives a comparative analysis of the performance of a wind turbine direct drive train system with PMSG and fully rated converters when two different wind turbine models are used for its assessment. The impact of the advanced Aero-Hydro-Servo-Elastic model, and the most common analytical function wind turbine model, on the generator-converter dynamics are assessed. Results corresponding to the system response to steps up/down in wind speed and turbulent wind speed conditions are presented and discussed in the paper. It is found that below rated speed there is no significant difference between results obtained from both models. Above rated wind speed there exist some differences among results.

articleTitle: Symmetrical VSC monopole scheme alternative grounding circuit arrangements
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: VSC symmetrical monopole grounding circuit with a focus on necessity of the grounding, overview of the existing topologies and a proposal of alternative grounding circuits is discussed in this paper. The key design concepts, advantages and challenges associated with the proposed alternative configurations are evaluated. The analysis includes comparison of the proposed solutions with the grounding methodologies implemented in practical applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of sub-synchronous control interaction for LCC using the generalized nyquist stability criterion
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In this work, the Sub-Synchronous Control Interaction (SSCI) phenomena is investigated in an ac-dc system consisting of a Line Commutated Converter (LCC) connected to the series compensated ac side using the Generalized Nyquist stability Criterion (GNC). To do this, the impedance response of the LCC together with the ac filters looking from the Point of Common Coupling (PCC) bus is first obtained from an improved LCC analytical model. The ac system includes a transmission line model in series with the series compensation capacitor. The impedance frequency response of the ac network is then obtained by exciting an Electromagnetic Transients (EMT) model of the ac network (after isolation from the converter) with a multi-sine signal current signal and conducting a Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) of the resulting voltage. With the impedance of both side available, GNC is employed to determine the Proposed "Harmonic Stability Margin (HSM)" index of the system. This is a measure of the propensity of the system to experience harmonic or sub-harmonic instability. The HSM is a function of the system parameters such as the controller gains, and especially has a linear relationship with Short Circuit Ratio (SCR). This allows easy determination of the critical SCR at the onset of instability from frequency response analysis at any other SCR value. The results are validated by EMT simulations.

articleTitle: A single pole to ground fault location method for HVDC transmission lines based on coupling characteristics
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In this paper, coupling coefficient between conductors is demonstrated as a superior indicator for single pole fault location. A method is proposed to locate faults via estimating the coupling coefficient with the help of single end current measurements taken within the first mille-second after the fault created wave reach the terminal. As the coupling coefficient is not dependent on fault resistance, the single pole fault location can be done with the help of pre-calculated inverse coupling coefficients estimated for some metallic faults applied at regular intervals. The performances of the proposed single end fault location scheme are evaluated in long bipole line commutated converter based HVdc transmission system as well as in a medium length monopole HVdc transmission configuration. Higher accuracy is observed despite of simplicity of the proposed scheme.

Author Keywords: Fault Location in HVDC Transmission Line

articleTitle: A new practical approach to evaluate critical gain for an HVDC based damping controller using wide area measurement system
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The paper proposes a comprehensive design approach for a robust wide area measurement system (WAMS) based inter-area swing mode (0.1Hz–1.0Hz) damping controller for networks with embedded multiple High-voltage Dc (HVDC) links. A simplified low-frequency model for the converter is first used to design the controller, which uses a specially designed feedback signal that greatly improves damping and is relatively robust against changes in operating point and loss of communication. However, the paper identifies a drawback, in that although using the simplified model does provide a good design, it can sometimes suggest unacceptable controller gains that cause instability. As predicted by the model, the damping of the targeted low frequency inter-area modes improves with increasing gain. However, if increased beyond a certain critical value, Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) simulation shows that the larger gain results in de-stabilization of the higher frequency modes of the converter. This is not predicted by the simplified representation in the design process which only considers the low-frequency converter behaviour. This critical gain can be determined using a generalized Nyquist criterion. This advocates a two-step process design. The simplified model can first be used for the basic design, and EMT simulation combined with Nyquist Analysis can then be used to determine the maximum limit for the controller gain.

articleTitle: Effects of windfarm curtailment on a 5-terminal VSC-HVDC network
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Multi-Terminal HVDC (MTDC) systems are the focus of research for the future of HVDC technology. However maintaining the stability of the MTDC network is currently an issue. This paper describes how a simplified state-space model of a multi-terminal network can be used to design robust droop power controllers. Using a five terminal network as the case study, the effect of windfarm curtailment for network stability was investigated. Results show that for most severe operation cases, windfarm curtailment successfully maintains system stability.

articleTitle: On the performance of the energy-controlled MMC: Impact of the internal and the DC capacitances in HVDC applications
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: As the power system is evolving towards a cleaner energy generation framework, the penetration of power electronic devices into the grid has become an evident fact. The number of commissioned VSC-HVDC installations is growing, and the MMC topology is gaining relevance in the field. The control of the MMC is well known to be challenging, and several efforts have been dedicated to this topic in the recent years. In this paper, the impact of the DC side and the internal capacitances of the MMC in terms of dynamic performance is analysed. An energy-based control approach is considered, and different control structures are discussed. In order to overcome the unsatisfactory performance of the MMC in some scenarios, a tuning methodology for the DC voltage and the total energy controllers is addressed via HL norm based optimal techniques. Simulations have been performed using a complete non-linear model of the system using MATLAB Simscape Power Systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of "Open Grid" protection strategy for a DC network
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: "Open Grid" protection strategy is proposed for protecting DC networks with converters that cannot block fault current and rely on DC circuit breakers. With this method, each DC circuit breaker (DC-CB), based on its own, local measurements (e.g. overcurrent, undervoltage) trips without discrimination. Using the same local measurements, the DC-CBs, discriminate "healthy" DC circuit(s) and re-close. This mainly aims to increase the speed of fault current interruption and reduce the duty of an individual DC-CB in blocking a fault. This paper develops the protection algorithms which can meet DC protection requirement with different fault types, locations and fault impedances. The analysis of the fault behaviour following the action of protection system in the event of a DC fault has also been given. Different DC fault characteristics have been described. Further validations of the robustness of the Open Grid via simulation models developed in PSCAD/EMTDC have been provided. Tests have shown that the Open Grid can successfully detect and discriminate DC faults in a meshed DC grid model.

articleTitle: A hybrid cascaded converter applicable for UHVDC transmission and feeding to load centre
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper proposes a new kind of hybrid cascaded converter for the UHVDC systems connected to load centres. The cascaded converter is formed by the MMCs in seriesparallel connection. When the cascaded converter is applied to the UHVDC system as the inverter, the system will combine the merits of hierarchical connection with asynchronous interconnection so as to strengthen the receiving system and makes the power distribution of the receiving system more flexible. The structure of the cascaded converter is introduced in detail. The control strategy is proposed. The specific operating modes and the strategy to switch operating modes are studied in detail, for which a certain amount of power transmission can be guaranteed when one of the sub-converters quit operation. Finally, a hybrid UHVDC system based on cascaded converter is built in PSCAD / EMTDC. The simulation verifies the availability of the system and control strategy. The results indicate that the cascaded converter has a good availability in UHVDC system feeding in intensive receiving systems.

articleTitle: Onshore grid frequency control using multi-terminal HVDC connected to full-scale converter for offshore wind generator and adjustable speed motor drive for offshore plant
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper proposes a new grid frequency control scheme, using an offshore wind farm and an offshore mining plant, linked to an onshore grid by way of a multi-terminal HVDC system. The originality of the proposed scheme is that both the power charged and discharged by the dc capacitor in the full-scale converter for the wind generator, and the power consumed by the induction motor for the mining plant are controlled, in accordance with the onshore grid frequency fluctuations. PSCAD simulation case studies were carried out for confirming the proposed scheme. The results revealed that the proposed scheme using the offshore facilities and HVDC system is valid for improving onshore grid frequency stability.

articleTitle: Wide area synchrophasor measurements based ac/dc integrated remedial action scheme for overload prevention
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper presents a measurement based Remedial Action Scheme for Manitoba Hydro Grid with multiple HVdc and HVac interconnections to prevent the overloading caused by the tripping of tie-lines under high export scenarios. The proposed scheme includes three stages. The first stage involves the identification of events, the second stage for the overload violation check and the third stage is to take emergency control actions. Remedial action is the fast control of HVDC power by modifying the converter set points. The proposed Remedial Action Scheme helps to prevent cascaded tripping due to line overload and ensures maximum power transfer. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the method proposed.

articleTitle: Inertia effect and load sharing capability of grid forming converters connected to a transmission grid
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The virtual synchronous machine concept (VSM) has been developed initially to reproduce the synchronous machine stabilizing effect by providing inertia with the emulation of swing equation, whereas droop control is developed initially to ensure load sharing and has no inertia. An introduction of a low pass filter to droop control has been motivated to filter the active power measurement and ensures a time decoupling with the inner control loops, whereas, this low-pass filter can also provide inertia to the system. This functionality is limited due to its negative impact on the active power dynamic. This paper proposes an analysis of the conventional droop control by showing its limitations and proposes an improved inertial droop control that allows providing the inertia to the system and ensures a good dynamic behavior of the active power at once in simple manner, and without modifying the load sharing capability. The results obtained are compared to the conventional method (Droop control and VSM) in various topologies in order to show the relevance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Assessment of passive islanding detection methods for DC microgrids
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper provides an assessment of passive islanding detection methods in DC microgrids. In order to analyse the response of a DC microgrid to an islanding event, DC voltage and current signatures are captured locally at the terminals of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs). Further analysis on DC voltage and current measurements is carried out to derive the Rate of Change of Voltage (ROCOV) and the Rate of Change of Current (ROCOC), to distinguish between genuine islanding events and other disturbances. A detailed DC microgrid has been developed in MATLAB/Simulink to analyse the response of the DERs within a DC microgrid during intentional or unintentional islanding events. The results show that these approaches cannot be used to classify and characterise between islanding and non-islanding events caused by high resistive faults for DC microgrids, as the response of the DERs are dependent on the technology and associated control systems, which influences post event analysis in distinguishing between events.

articleTitle: Solid state transformer: An overview of circuit configurations and applications
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper first outlined the motivation behind solid state transformer (SST) against conventional line frequency transformer (LFT) as well as its functional futures and benefits and secondly explore all the possible configurations of SST in terms of circuit configurations, advantages, disadvantages and their potential areas of applications. Four circuit configurations considered in this paper include; single stage SST, two stage SST with low voltage DC link (LVDC), two stage SST with high voltage DC link (HVDC) and three stage SST. Our findings reveals that apart from providing voltage regulation, SST can provide other additional ancillary services to the grid to enable it cope with transients. These services (such as power quality improvement, fault isolation, instantaneous voltage regulation, active and reactive power compensation) are not offered by LFT, as such SST is considered as the potential transformer in smart grid applications, renewable energy integration, modern traction systems and other applications where space and volume are critical.

articleTitle: Design, construction and testing of a modular multilevel converter with a distributed control architecture
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Many simplified modular multilevel converter prototypes have been developed over the past few years, typically in order to demonstrate high level control schemes. Many of these prototypes are based on conventional centralised control strategies and are therefore unable to address concerns regarding scalability and the limitations imposed by hardware delays when using distributed control strategies. This paper presents an overview of common control architectures along with the design, construction and initial findings from industrially representative control hardware.

articleTitle: Power system stability enhancement via VSC-HVDC control using remote signals: Application on the Nordic 44-bus test system
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: In this paper the benefits of embedded VSC-HVDC links with supplementary controls for small-signal stability enhancement purposes using remote signals, is studied and applied on the Nordic Grid. Firstly the structure of phasor models for the study of large power systems is presented. A current injection model of the VSC-HVDC link suitable for phasor simulation of large-scale power system is presented. For the analysis and simulations, the tools developed during the iTesla project are used to assess the stability of different operating points of the Nordic Grid. The studied operating points are found based using the actual power flow data of the real system provided by the Nordic44-Nordpool repository. Through small signal analysis the most weakly damped oscillation modes of the system are identified. Based on the computation of the participation factors, the nature of the oscillations are identified and also for the unstable operating points the sources of instability are determined. Finally a control based on the measurement of remote signals is implemented for the modulation of the active power of the embedded HVDC link with the aim of improving the stability of the system.

articleTitle: Coordination of mechanical DCCBs and temporary blocking of half bridge MMC
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper proposes a dc grid protection strategy based on temporary MMC blocking in combination with mechanical DCCBs on dc lines. MMCs are blocked for only a short period of time while DCCBs operate and resume operation afterwards. A comparison is made with a protection strategy in which MMC blocking is avoided. The study analyses the impact of dc faults on dc power flow, ac system, DCCB dimensioning and MMC's antiparallel diodes. Operation is demonstrated on a point-to-point HVDC and a three-terminal dc grid, also using thermal model of MMC's IGBT module. Main benefits of the proposed strategy are simplicity and low protection system cost. On the downside, antiparallel diodes are exposed to greater current and thermal stress.

articleTitle: Implementation of a dedicated control to limit adverse interaction in multi-vendor HVDC systems
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper reports on recent work performed in the framework of European project Best Paths DEMO #2, where interoperability in multi-vendor VSC-HVDC systems is investigated. In this four-year project, three major HVDC suppliers provided detailed EMT models which implement their state-of-the-art VSC technology in order to comply with realistic requirements and test cases provided by European TSOs and academics. Those models were used to perform interoperability studies and assess to what extent available technology is interoperable between various competitors. This paper provides the definition of ‘interoperability’ as agreed among the various stakeholders and describes the methodology used in the project for its assessment. It also reports on the results observed using detailed EMT converter models provided by the vendors, some of which exhibiting interoperability issues. In particular, some oscillatory behaviours were observed for which no satisfactory fix could be implemented directly in the converter models. Therefore, an innovative solution was implemented and tested, based on a DC-side Power Oscillation Damping (POD) control implemented in a third-party control in charge of the coordination of the converters; this proved to be most beneficial and finally limited the impact of those interoperability issues. Finally, the relevance and practical implementation of this solution is discussed and compared to direct adaptations in the converters themselves.

articleTitle: Modelling of VSC-HVDC multi-terminal systems for small-signal angle stability analysis
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper presents a model for small-signal analysis (SSA) of the angle stability of hybrid high-voltage AC (HVAC) systems containing high-voltage DC multi-terminal systems based on Voltage Source Converters (VSC-HVDC). The model developed is highly flexible and makes it possible to seamlessly adapt existing tools for SSA of HVAC systems to be used for hybrid HVAC/VSC-HVDC systems. The proposed small-signal model has been validated and has been used to analyse the impact of an active-power control strategy on power oscillations. The strategy was previously used to improve transient stability in the same type of systems. Results show that the strategy analysed can also help to damp inter-area power oscillations.

articleTitle: The impact of MVDC upon conventional distance protection schemes in hybrid ac-dc distribution networks
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper looks at the protection implications of introducing fully controllable, embedded, medium voltage dc (MVDC) power electronic links into power distribution networks. Studies have indicated, protection notwithstanding, that embedded MVDC can be used to provide economically attractive, enhanced capacity and control of power flows. Through a series of simulation studies, the impact on distance protection schemes (in terms of reach and response time) resulting from the introduction of a controlled MVDC link have been examined for symmetrical faults. The paper also considers under what conditions a dc side fault can be observed from the ac grid. A series of recommendations for system integrators are made.

articleTitle: A new test circuit for operational testing of HVDC valves
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Type tests for valves for HVDC converters are defined in IEC 60700-1 (for LCC valves) and IEC 62501 (for VSC valves). Of the tests described therein, the operational tests (which demonstrate the ability of the valve to withstand the repetitive voltage and current stresses occurring alternately during normal operation) are challenging and require a very specialised test circuit. For LCC valves the established technique has been to use a synthetic test circuit while for VSC valves the use of some form of back-to-back test circuit is common. Both methods have limitations, however, and a brand-new test facility, operating on different principles, has recently been commissioned. Its operation for both LCC mode and VSC mode is described in the paper.

articleTitle: Impact of the DC circuit breaker design on selective fault detection and clearing methods in multi-terminal HVDC systems
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Multi-terminal HVDC (MTDC) systems have been identified as a new and effective means to interconnect areas of vast renewable generation infeed with load centres. To guarantee high system availability and supply reliability, DC transmission line faults need to be detected, localised and cleared with minimum impact on the overall system operation. In particular, false tripping of healthy lines and blocking of converter stations may cause cascading outages and should therefore be avoided. In recent years, several DC circuit breaker (DCCB) concepts have been proposed as a possibility to enable the separation of faulted MTDC systems parts. However, the converter behaviour is often neglected when studying the fault clearing process. This paper therefore focuses on the impacts of DCCB design criteria on voltage and current characteristics during DC line faults and evaluates the feasibility and limitations for DCCB-based line protection with respect to continued system operation. Electromagnetic transient fault simulations are carried out in a representative MTDC system for different DCCB current ratings, dead times and DC reactor values. Based on prospective fault characteristics at the line ends, maximum available detection times and thresholds for current-based and voltage-based line protection methods are derived. As the results indicate, fault separation with continued system operation of healthy system parts can only be achieved for certain breaker designs. Insufficiently sized DC reactors, breaking times of several milliseconds or limited DCCB and converter ratings may lead to false tripping or undesired converter blocking.

articleTitle: A calculation method for steady-state short-circuit currents in multi-terminal HVDC-grids
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Multi-terminal HVDC grids will be an important part of the energy system of the future. For their design, the knowledge of the prospective short-circuit currents is key. However, there currently is no standard for the calculation of these currents. As a basis for such a standard, this paper proposes a calculation method for steady-state short-circuit currents. Using piecewise linear VI-characteristics, the nonlinear network can be solved by an iterative algorithm. The proposed calculation method can be applied to HVDC networks with arbitrary topology, dif­ferent converter types and all types of DC faults. The accuracy of the results is demonstrated relative to existing calculation methods and detailed simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Filterless line commutated converter for HVDC transmission
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Conventionally, Line Commutated Converter (LCC) technology for High Voltage DC (HVDC) transmission incorporates AC filters to remove the harmonics generated from converter operation. Traditionally, the filters also provide reactive power support. However, AC filters and the associated switchgear are known to be bulky and this translates to increased CAPEX. This paper presents a new converter topology which incorporates a six-pulse thyristor bridge with a Voltage Source Converter (VSC) STATCOM valves connected at the transformer secondary terminals. The STATCOM valves provide AC current control at the transformer's secondary windings. Additionally, the STATCOM valves control the thyristor commutation process irrespective of secondary AC voltage. In order to provide distortion free current at the AC primary windings, two six-pulse converters are connected in a 12-pulse configuration, which provides distortion-free sinusoidal currents at the primary side. The topology therefore minimises the need for bulky AC filters and is also able to provide reactive power support to the AC network. The paper shows the analytical model, converter waveforms and a commercial benchmarking showing the potential of the proposed approach vs. conventional LCC technology.

articleTitle: Analysis of overvoltage levels in the rigid bipolar MMC-HVDC configuration
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Bipolar high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission systems based on modular multilevel converters (MMC) are intended to be used in several upcoming projects. This contribution performs a profound analysis of occurring overvoltages in a single point grounded rigid bipolar transmission scheme, where the MMC topology equipped with half-bridge (HB) submodules is utilized. In order to derive voltage stresses affecting the dc cable system, a detailed parametric study is performed by means of time­domain simulations. Obtained results are discussed with regard to different station grounding configurations.

articleTitle: Virtual capacitor control for stability improvement of HVDC system comprising DC reactors
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: Presently, HVDC circuit breakers (DCCBs) rely on relatively large DC reactors to limit the rate of rise of fault current. However, such additional passive components can significantly deteriorate the stability of the HVDC grids. This paper first analyzes the underlying instability issue attributed to the DC reactor by using a simplified converter station model, which reveals that the DC-link capacitor can compensate for the detrimental effect of the DC reactor and increase the stability margin. This capacitor, however, is usually avoided and distributed over the capacitors in sub-modules in the state-of-the-art Modular Multilevel Converters (MMCs). Thus, the authors make use of the previously proposed Virtual Capacitor Control, which enables the MMCs to emulate the dynamics of the capacitor by using the energy stored in the distributed capacitors. A smallsignal stability analysis of an MMC station model, including control loops, a DC reactor, and frequency-dependent HVDC cables, corroborates the unstable behavior of the system in the presence of a large DC reactor and demonstrates a drastic improvement of the stability by the virtual capacitor control. The validity of the proposed control is confirmed by electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations of a detailed MMC model with 400 SMs per arm.

articleTitle: Analysis of hybrid LCC-VSC HVDC transmission system configurations
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: HVDC transmission systems are based on two main converter technologies: Line Commutated Converters (LCCs) and Voltage Source Converters (VSCs). LCC-based systems were introduced first and represent most of the current HVDC transmission. VSC-based systems were introduced more recently and provide higher operational flexibility compared to LCC. However, LCC is still the preferred option for bulk power transmission due to higher voltage and current capabilities. Hybrid HVDC configurations with LCCs and VSCs represent a potential solution where the advantages of both technologies can be combined. This paper analyses hybrid HVDC link configurations defined from the combination of possible control modes and converter location. The start-up process and converter control design in normal operation are presented for each configuration. Also, the potential applications and advantages and disadvantages of all hybrid HVDC configurations are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Installation and interfacing HVDC control replicas at the national HVDC centre
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The National HVDC Centre (HVDC Centre), located in Scotland, UK; is a simulation and training facility that supports all HVDC schemes connecting to Great Britain's (GB) electricity network. The HVDC Centre has installed replica control hardware for a multi-terminal enabled HVDC scheme under construction in the north of Scotland, the Caithness-Moray HVDC project, (CM Project). This enables real-time modelling to resolve potential issues and mitigate any impact on the delivery and operation of the CM project. This paper describes the practicalities of: specifying, testing, installing and interfacing these replicas, with a real-time simulator, at the HVDC Centre which was completed in August 2018. This paper also describes the subsequent use of the installed replicas to prove and test control measures required for integration of the CM HVDC scheme with the AC Network; together with a quantification of the value of the benefits that replicas provide to HVDC projects and to grid operation.

articleTitle: Simulation and experimental study on application principles of high power PP-IGBT in the DC circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: As an emerging type of electrical equipment, design and testing of DC circuit breaker face enormous challenges. Hybrid DC circuit breaker is one of mainstream design solutions, and its commutation branch is normally based on power switches typically press-pack IGBTs. The characteristics of IGBTs are generally well understood for converter applications, however special setup or arrangement for IGBTs are needed when they are used in a DC circuit breaker, so that they can withstand and turn off very high DC short circuit fault current. This study starts with general working principle of DC circuit breakers, and then introduces core requirements on press-pack IGBTs when used in the commutation branch of a hybrid DC circuit breaker. Furthermore, by looking into internal structure of press-pack IGBT, manual calculation and simulation analysis of IGBT junction temperature and lab bench demonstration testing, key measures or arrangement for press-pack IGBT in DC circuit breaker application have been studied. Finally, the full-scale testing from a third party, in which a 19kA DC fault current is turned off using a single 4.5kV/3kA press-pack IGBT, proves effectiveness of proposed key measures for press-pack IGBT when used in DC circuit breakers.

articleTitle: Compensation of the voltage fluctuations in the distribution network of london underground using the SVC PLUS®
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper is focused on the voltage fluctuations in the electrical network of London Underground (LU). For this purpose LU's network was modelled in DigSILENT PowerFactory software. The Voltage Fluctuation Study was a part of the project, whose main objective was an installation of the ±37 MVAr Siemens STATCOM (SVC PLUS®) at an existing LU Power Station connected to LU's 22kV network. Therefore, the voltage fluctuation assessment has been performed for both configurations of this network: (i) without SVC PLUS® and (ii) with SVC PLUS®. Thus, the impact of the SVC PLUS® on the voltage quality was assessed.

articleTitle: Reliability and economic evaluation of high voltage direct current interconnectors for large-scale renewable energy integration and transmission
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: This paper outlines a methodology for assessing the reliability and cost of operating multi-terminal High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission interconnectors with a comparison being drawn on the benefits of using modular multilevel converters (MMC). The MMCs random failure/repair processes are modelled as either a two-state or three-state Markov processes. A time-sequential Monte Carlo simulation is used to simulate the operation of the modified IEEE Reliability Test System (RTS) with the MMC-HVDC interconnectors, over a one-year period. The RTS accommodates variable wind generation, and the results confirm the use of HVDC as tie lines provide geographical aggregation, allowing for much greater penetration of variable generation in the connected systems. The three-state MMC model, in addition to the binary up and down states, consists of a derated state in which the converter voltage is reduced to 57.7% of its nominal voltage. The additional state was found to reduce the downtime of the link by 89.6%, increasing the available flow capacity by 458 GWh/year. The increase flow capacity leads to an increase in arbitrage revenue of €3.17m per year and a reduction in project payback time of 1.5 years.

articleTitle: Provision of fast frequency response by SVC plus frequency stabilizer
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
abstract: The frequency of the power system must lie within a predefined range to maintain the operational security of the power system. Synchronous generators with their rotating masses help to resist changes in system frequency. However as renewable generation is replacing conventional generation, the ability of the system to resist changes in frequency decreases. The decreasing system inertia in the future grids is prompting the TSOs to look for better frequency response services like Enhanced Frequency Response (EFR). This paper presents an approach of power intensive energy storage in the form of supercapacitors to damp the frequency within 10 seconds of the frequency deviation. The solution is evaluated for the transmission grid models of UK, Ireland and Hawaii with a focus on the UK grid. The lowest frequency point, f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nadir</inf> and the excursions outside operational and statutory frequency limits are evaluated for all grids with and without the solution.

articleTitle: Multi-zone LVDC distribution systems architecture for facilitating low carbon technologies uptake
publicationTitle: 15th IET International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission (ACDC 2019)
